qs.q: A 62-year-old man presents with a hard, irregular prostate nodule on digital rectal examination and a total PSA of 8.5 ng/mL. His transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsies show acinar adenocarcinoma. In which zone of the prostate did this malignancy most likely originate?
qs.e: Over 95% of prostate cancers are adenocarcinomas arising mainly in the peripheral zone, which allows them to be palpable on digital rectal examination. The transition zone is where benign prostatic hyperplasia typically develops, causing early urinary symptoms.
qs.s: Prostate Cancer: Screening, Diagnosis, Staging and Treatment: MCQs

qs.q: A 61-year-old man is evaluated for urinary symptoms. His serum PSA is 5.0 ng/mL, transrectal ultrasound shows a prostate volume of 50 cc, yielding a calculated PSA density of 0.10 ng/mL/cc. Which of the following best interprets this density value?
o: It falls below the threshold that typically suggests cancer
It confirms the presence of a high-grade PI-RADS 5 lesion
It indicates a free-to-total ratio below fourteen percent
It represents a velocity increase exceeding normal limits
qs.e: A PSA density over 0.15 ng/mL/cc suggests cancer, making a value of 0.10 below the typical suspicion threshold. PSA density helps differentiate benign enlargement from true malignancy by adjusting for prostate size.
qs.s: Prostate Cancer: Screening, Diagnosis, Staging and Treatment: MCQs
